newsitem.title: UK: Euroshare rally boosted by Wall St gains.
newsitem.headline: Euroshare rally boosted by Wall St gains.

text.p: European shares extended their morning rally on Friday when Wall Street surged in early trade with technology shares leading the way.

Europe's three key bourses, London, Frankfurt and Paris, were up 0.64, 1.22 and 0.81 percent, respectively, just before 1500 gmt, at which point Wall Street's Dow Jones industrial average was up almost 40 points, or 0.6 percent.
The U.S.'s Nasdaq Composite index sailed up 10.7, or 0.84 percent, to 1291.4, in early trade erasing its steep losses on Thursday when it closed off 10.33 at 1280.70.
The Nasdaq index contains many of the technology stocks which were slammed yesterday on fears of poor holiday sales at computer retailers.

Earlier, European shares romped higher in the wake of Wall Street's impressive rally on Thursday when it recovered from being 96 points down to close just 5.78 points after New Year bargain hunters came out in force.
Friday's Wall Street surge was a continuation of the strong buying seen late on Thursday as programme buying kicked in.

"A lot of people that weren't working decided to call in late and say, "Start buying these things'," Robert Froehlich, chief investment strategist at Van Kampen American Capital, said of Wall Street's performance on Thursday.
U.S. shares remain prey to fears that too rapid growth in the world's number one economy might lead to higher interest rates, which would undermine soaring share valuations, however.
Stronger-than-expected U.S. construction spending in November, which the Commerce Department said rose by 1.9 percent, could renew these worries.
By 1500, London shares were near the day's best levels with the FTSE 100 26 points up at 4,083.4, though volume was thin and traders said many players were still on holiday.
French stocks also chased Wall Street higher, extending their earlier gains.
The blue-chip CAC-40 index, which had traded nervously in the morning, was up 18.17 points at 2,275.14.

Earlier, French shares also received a small boost from the government's nomination to the Bank of France monetary policy council of two candidates viewed as favourable to easier interest rates, brokers said.
The government nominated Pierre Guillen and Jean-Rene Bernard, replacing two outgoing members -- including Jean Boissonnat -- viewed as being from the strong franc camp.
Germany's DAX share index ended bourse trade slightly higher, boosted by interest from German domestic fund managers and a strong performance from German Bunds.
At the end of the session the DAX-30 index of German blue-chip shares stood at 2,859.28 points, up 10.51 points.

"The German market seems to be in better shape than other markets. There seems to be German domestic funds committing cash -- they have been light on equities so far and now they seem to be putting some money in," said one trader.
Germany's electronically traded Ibis DAX index mirrored Wall Street more accurately however and was up 34.52 at 2,855.33 points.
In currencies, the dollar also extended its morning gains and stood at 1.5555 marks and 116.00 yen by midafternoon.
"People are generally quite bullish on the dollar," said a corporate dealer at German bank. Traders also said the dollar's recovery on Friday was led by a climb in sterling.
Gold, sometimes seen as a hedge against inflation, fell further in afternoon trading, with traders puzzled by its weakness in the face of concern that inflation might re-emerge.
CURRENCIES AT 1500 GMT
The dollar stood at 1.5555 marks and 116.00 yen, compared with 1.5407 and 115.47 in late trade on Thursday.
STOCK MARKETS AT 1500 GMT
The FTSE 100 index of leading British shares rose 26.0 points to 4,083.4.
The 30-share DAX index in Frankfurt was up 10.51 at 2,859.28.
In Paris, the CAC-40 share index rose 18.17 to 2,275.14.
PRECIOUS METALS
Gold was fixed at $364.00, down from the morning's fix of $364.30 and London's close on Thursday of $366.85.
